purpose: Classify disputes and applications concerning correction, rectification, alteration or other challenges to registered property records without assuming that an alleged error automatically changes title.
legal_distinctions: An alleged error does not itself establish that the register is legally incorrect.
Rectification, alteration, court intervention and compensation are distinct questions.
A registry map or folio issue may require separate boundary, title and historical-record analysis.
Fraud or forgery allegations require evidence and may trigger separate legal and procedural routes.
A current register entry must be distinguished from historical entries and the underlying instrument.
Correction of a record and determination of the underlying substantive dispute are not always the same process.
evidence_requirements: underlying instrument or deed where relevant
title plan and boundary evidence where relevant
court order or judgment where applicable
documentary evidence supporting the alleged error
date and procedural history of prior applications
official_routes: Courts Service where judicial determination is required
guardrails: Never state that the register is wrong without evidence.
Never alter or reinterpret a title result merely because a user disputes it.
Never treat rectification as automatically available without checking the applicable statutory route.
Never infer fraud or forgery from an inconsistency alone.
Never collapse compensation and rectification into one remedy.
Property-specific disputes require verified records and, where necessary, professional or judicial review.
